part0_abstract_claims: After subtraction of the model, the residuals showed an approximate linear upward trend after 1942.
The resulting full natural plus anthropogenic model fits the entire 160 year record very well.
Residual analysis does not provide any evidence for a substantial cooling effect due to sulfate aerosols from 1940 to 1970.
The cooling observed during that period may be due to a natural 60-year cycle
New solar activity proxy models are developed that suggest a mechanism for both the 60-year climate cycle and a portion of the long-term warming trend.
Our results suggest that ... the anthropogenic contribution to climate change since 1970 should be around half of that previously claimed by the IPCC [2007].
A 21st Century forecast suggests that climate may warm less than 1 ºC by 2100.
